<div class="priority-title">
    <h2>â­â­â­â­ High Priority</h2>
    <div class="line"></div>
</div>


<!-- Q11 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 11</div>

    <h3>What are the main components of a VPC?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ COMMON
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        Important VPC-related components include:

        <br><br>

        â†’ VPC

        <br>
        â†’ Subnets

        <br>
        â†’ Route Tables

        <br>
        â†’ Internet Gateway

        <br>
        â†’ NAT Gateway

        <br>
        â†’ Security Groups

        <br>
        â†’ Network ACLs

        <br>
        â†’ Network Interfaces

        <br>
        â†’ VPC Endpoints

        <br>
        â†’ VPC Peering

        <br>
        â†’ Transit Gateway for larger network designs

    </p>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "A VPC consists of networking constructs such as
            CIDR ranges, subnets, route tables, gateways,
            security controls and network interfaces. Additional
            connectivity components such as VPC endpoints,
            peering and Transit Gateway can be used depending
            on the architecture."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q12 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 12</div>

    <h3>What is a VPC Peering connection?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ IMPORTANT
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        VPC Peering is a networking connection between two VPCs
        that allows resources in those VPCs to communicate
        using private IP addresses, subject to routing and
        security configuration.

        The VPCs can be in the same or different AWS accounts,
        and supported peering can also span Regions.

    </p>

    <div class="flow">

        VPC-A

        â‡„

        VPC Peering

        â‡„

        VPC-B

    </div>

    <div class="important">

        âš ï¸ The VPC CIDR ranges must not overlap for normal VPC
        peering routing to work.

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "VPC Peering creates private network connectivity
            between two VPCs. After establishing the peering
            connection, we must configure appropriate routes
            and security rules. The VPC CIDRs should not overlap."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q13 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 13</div>

    <h3>What is a VPC Endpoint?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ VERY USEFUL
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        VPC Endpoints provide private connectivity from a VPC
        to supported AWS services without requiring traffic to
        traverse the public internet.

        Two important endpoint categories are:

        <br><br>

        <strong>Gateway Endpoints</strong>

        <br>
        Commonly used for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.

        <br><br>

        <strong>Interface Endpoints</strong>

        <br>
        Powered by AWS PrivateLink and implemented using
        elastic network interfaces.

    </p>

    <div class="example">

        <strong>ðŸ’¡ DevOps Example</strong>

        <p>

            A private EC2 instance needs access to S3.

            Instead of sending that traffic through a NAT
            Gateway, an S3 Gateway Endpoint can provide
            private access.

        </p>

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "VPC endpoints provide private connectivity between
            resources in a VPC and supported AWS services.
            Gateway endpoints are commonly used for S3 and
            DynamoDB, while interface endpoints use AWS
            PrivateLink."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q14 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 14</div>

    <h3>What is an Elastic Network Interface (ENI)?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ IMPORTANT
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        An ENI is a virtual network interface in a VPC.

        It can have attributes such as:

        <br><br>

        â†’ Private IPv4 addresses

        <br>
        â†’ Secondary private IP addresses

        <br>
        â†’ Security groups

        <br>
        â†’ MAC address

        <br>
        â†’ Optional public/Elastic IP associations

    </p>

    <div class="example">

        <strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Understanding</strong>

        <p>

            Think of an ENI as a virtual network card attached
            to a resource.

        </p>

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "An Elastic Network Interface is a virtual network
            interface in a VPC that provides network connectivity
            and can have private IP addresses, security groups
            and other network attributes."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q15 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 15</div>

    <h3>What is the difference between a NAT Gateway and an Internet Gateway?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON
    </span>

    <div class="flow">

        Internet Gateway

        â†’

        VPC â†” Internet

        <br><br>

        NAT Gateway

        â†’

        Private Subnet â†’ Internet

        <br>

        ðŸš« No direct unsolicited inbound access

    </div>

    <p class="answer">

        An <strong>Internet Gateway</strong> is attached to a
        VPC and provides a path for internet communication.

        A <strong>NAT Gateway</strong> is deployed in a subnet,
        typically a public subnet, and allows private subnet
        resources to make outbound internet connections.

    </p>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "An Internet Gateway provides internet connectivity
            for a VPC. A NAT Gateway is used by private subnet
            resources to initiate outbound internet connections
            without exposing those resources with public IPs."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q16 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 16</div>

    <h3>Why is a NAT Gateway placed in a public subnet?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ TRICKY
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        A NAT Gateway needs a path to the internet for the
        outbound traffic it translates.

        Therefore, for IPv4 internet access, the NAT Gateway
        is typically deployed in a public subnet with a route
        to an Internet Gateway and an Elastic IP.

        Private subnet route tables then point their default
        route to the NAT Gateway.

    </p>

    <div class="flow">

        Private Subnet

        â†’

        NAT Gateway

        â†’

        Public Subnet

        â†’

        IGW

        â†’

        Internet

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "A NAT Gateway is placed in a public subnet because
            it needs a route through the Internet Gateway to
            provide outbound internet connectivity for resources
            in private subnets."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q17 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 17</div>

    <h3>What is VPC Flow Logs?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ MONITORING + TROUBLESHOOTING
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        VPC Flow Logs capture information about IP traffic
        going to and from network interfaces, subnets or VPCs
        depending on the configured scope.

        They are useful for troubleshooting connectivity and
        security analysis.

    </p>

    <div class="example">

        <strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

        <p>

            An application cannot connect to a database.

            Flow Logs can help determine whether traffic is
            being accepted or rejected at the network-flow
            level.

        </p>

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "VPC Flow Logs capture metadata about network
            traffic flows and are useful for troubleshooting
            connectivity, analyzing rejected traffic and
            supporting security investigations."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q18 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 18</div>

    <h3>What is a default route?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ COMMON
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        A default route is used when no more specific route
        matches the destination.

        For IPv4:

    </p>

    <pre>
```

0.0.0.0/0 </pre>

```
    <p class="answer">

        For IPv6:

    </p>

    <pre>
```

::/0 </pre>

```
    <div class="example">

        <strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

        <p>

            A public subnet route table might contain:

        </p>

        <pre>
```

0.0.0.0/0 â†’ Internet Gateway </pre>

```
    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "A default route matches destinations for which
            no more specific route exists. In IPv4 it is
            represented as 0.0.0.0/0."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>

            to connect multiple VPCs and on-premises networks.
            It simplifies large-scale network connectivity
            compared with maintaining many individual peering
            connections."

        </p>

<!-- Q21 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 21</div>

    <h3>What is an Elastic IP?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­ COMMON
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        An Elastic IP is a static public IPv4 address allocated
        to your AWS account.

        It can be associated with supported AWS resources.

        It is useful when a stable public IPv4 address is
        required.

    </p>

    <div class="important">

        âš ï¸ In production, avoid using Elastic IPs unnecessarily.
        DNS and load balancers are often better architectural
        choices for application endpoints.

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "An Elastic IP is a static public IPv4 address
            allocated to an AWS account that can be associated
            with supported resources when a stable public
            address is required."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q22 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 22</div>

    <h3>Can two VPCs have overlapping CIDR ranges?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­ TRICKY
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        Two completely independent VPCs can technically have
        the same CIDR range.

        However, overlapping CIDRs create problems for direct
        private routing between those networks and are
        generally avoided when designing connected networks.

    </p>

    <div class="example">

        <strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

        <p>

            VPC-A â†’ 10.0.0.0/16

            <br>

            VPC-B â†’ 10.0.0.0/16

            <br><br>

            If we later need normal VPC peering between them,
            the overlapping ranges prevent the required
            routing.

        </p>

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "Independent VPCs can have overlapping CIDRs, but
            overlapping address ranges prevent normal private
            routing between them and create major connectivity
            problems. Therefore non-overlapping CIDRs are
            preferred for connected network designs."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Q23 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">QUESTION 23</div>

    <h3>What is the difference between public IP and private IP in a VPC?</h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­ IMPORTANT
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        A <strong>private IP</strong> is used for communication
        inside the VPC and connected private networks.

        A <strong>public IPv4</strong> address is used for
        internet-facing communication when the network
        configuration allows it.

        Private IP addresses remain associated with the ENI
        while the instance exists, subject to the specific
        network configuration.

    </p>

    <div class="flow">

        Private IP

        â†’

        ðŸ  Internal Communication

        <br><br>

        Public IP

        â†’

        ðŸŒ Internet Communication

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "Private IP addresses are used for communication
            within the VPC and connected private networks.
            Public IPv4 addresses provide internet-facing
            addressing when the resource's routing and security
            configuration permits it."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>

    <h2>ðŸŽ¯ Real-Time VPC Scenarios</h2>

<!-- Scenario 1 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">SCENARIO 01</div>

    <h3>
        An EC2 instance in a private subnet cannot access the internet. How do you troubleshoot it?
    </h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        I would check the path step by step.

        <br><br>

        <strong>1. Check the private subnet route table.</strong>

        <br>

        It should have a default route:

    </p>

    <pre>
```

0.0.0.0/0 â†’ NAT Gateway </pre>

```
    <p class="answer">

        <strong>2. Check the NAT Gateway.</strong>

        <br>

        Confirm it is available and deployed in a public
        subnet.

        <br><br>

        <strong>3. Check the NAT subnet route.</strong>

        <br>

        NAT Gateway's subnet should have:

    </p>

    <pre>
```

0.0.0.0/0 â†’ Internet Gateway </pre>

```
    <p class="answer">

        <strong>4. Check Network ACLs.</strong>

        <br>

        Because NACLs are stateless, return traffic must also
        be allowed.

        <br><br>

        <strong>5. Check security group rules.</strong>

        <br>

        Verify required outbound traffic is allowed.

    </p>

    <div class="flow">

        Private EC2

        â†’

        Private Route Table

        â†’

        NAT Gateway

        â†’

        Public Route Table

        â†’

        IGW

        â†’

        Internet

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "I would first check the private subnet route table
            for a default route to the NAT Gateway. Then I would
            verify the NAT Gateway is healthy and is in a public
            subnet whose route table has a route to the Internet
            Gateway. Finally I would check NACL and security
            group rules."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Scenario 2 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">SCENARIO 02</div>

    <h3>
        EC2 has a public IP but still cannot access the internet. What will you check?
    </h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­â­ TROUBLESHOOTING
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        A public IP alone does not guarantee internet connectivity.

        I would check:

        <br><br>

        1. Is the subnet actually public?

        <br>

        2. Does its route table contain:

    </p>

    <pre>
```

0.0.0.0/0 â†’ Internet Gateway </pre>

```
    <p class="answer">

        3. Is the Internet Gateway attached to the VPC?

        <br>

        4. Are security group rules correct?

        <br>

        5. Are NACL rules correct?

        <br>

        6. Is the OS firewall blocking the traffic?

        <br>

        7. Is the application listening on the expected port?

    </p>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "I would not assume that a public IP is sufficient.
            I would verify the subnet route table, Internet
            Gateway attachment, security groups, NACLs,
            operating-system firewall and application listener."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Scenario 3 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">SCENARIO 03</div>

    <h3>
        Two EC2 instances in the same VPC cannot communicate. What would you check?
    </h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­â­ COMMON
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        I would check:

        <br><br>

        â†’ Are both instances in the expected VPC?

        <br>

        â†’ Are their subnets correctly routed?

        <br>

        â†’ Is the local VPC route present?

        <br>

        â†’ Does the destination security group allow the
        source?

        <br>

        â†’ Are NACLs allowing both directions?

        <br>

        â†’ Is the application actually listening?

        <br>

        â†’ Is the OS firewall blocking the connection?

    </p>

    <div class="example">

        <strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

        <p>

            Web Server:

            <br>
            10.0.1.10

            <br><br>

            Application Server:

            <br>
            10.0.2.10

            <br><br>

            If the application server's security group does not
            allow the required application port from the web
            server's security group, the connection can fail.

        </p>

    </div>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "I would verify the VPC and routing first, then
            check the destination security group, NACLs,
            operating-system firewall and application listener."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Scenario 4 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">SCENARIO 04</div>

    <h3>
        Design a production 3-tier architecture using VPC.
    </h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS ARCHITECTURE
    </span>

    <div class="flow">

        ðŸŒ Internet

        â†“

        âš–ï¸ Application Load Balancer

        â†“

        â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”

        â”‚ Public Subnets               â”‚

        â”‚ ALB                          â”‚

        â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜

        â†“

        â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”

        â”‚ Private App Subnets          â”‚

        â”‚ EC2 / ECS / Applications     â”‚

        â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜

        â†“

        â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”

        â”‚ Private DB Subnets           â”‚

        â”‚ Database                     â”‚

        â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜

    </div>

    <p class="answer">

        A common production design separates workloads into
        different subnet tiers.

        <br><br>

        <strong>Public subnet:</strong>

        <br>
        Load Balancer

        <br><br>

        <strong>Private application subnet:</strong>

        <br>
        Application servers

        <br><br>

        <strong>Private database subnet:</strong>

        <br>
        Database services

        <br><br>

        NAT Gateway can provide outbound internet access for
        private application resources when required.

        Multiple Availability Zones should be used for
        resilience.

    </p>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "I would design a multi-AZ VPC with public subnets
            for the load balancer, private application subnets
            for application workloads and isolated private
            database subnets. NAT Gateways can provide outbound
            internet access for private application resources,
            while security groups control tier-to-tier access."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>


<!-- Scenario 5 -->

<article class="question">

    <div class="question-number">SCENARIO 05</div>

    <h3>
        Security Group allows traffic, but the connection is still failing. What could be wrong?
    </h3>

    <span class="label">
        â­â­â­â­ TROUBLESHOOTING
    </span>

    <p class="answer">

        A Security Group is only one part of the network path.

        I would also check:

        <br><br>

        â†’ Route tables

        <br>
        â†’ NACLs

        <br>
        â†’ Internet Gateway / NAT Gateway

        <br>
        â†’ DNS

        <br>
        â†’ OS firewall

        <br>
        â†’ Application listener

        <br>
        â†’ Correct IP and port

        <br>
        â†’ VPC Flow Logs

    </p>

    <div class="interview-answer">

        <strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

        <p>

            "A security group being correct does not guarantee
            connectivity. I would verify routing, NACLs, gateways,
            DNS, the operating-system firewall and whether the
            application is listening on the expected address
            and port."

        </p>

    </div>

</article>

    <strong>ðŸ§  VPC One-Minute Revision</strong>

    <br><br>

    <strong>
        VPC = Your logical network in AWS
        <br><br>

        CIDR = IP address range
        <br><br>

        Subnet = Smaller network inside VPC
        <br><br>

        Public Subnet = Route to Internet Gateway
        <br><br>

        Private Subnet = No direct route to Internet Gateway
        <br><br>

        Route Table = Decides where traffic goes
        <br><br>

        Internet Gateway = VPC â†” Internet path
        <br><br>

        NAT Gateway = Private subnet â†’ outbound Internet
        <br><br>

        Security Group = Stateful resource-level firewall
        <br><br>

        NACL = Stateless subnet-level firewall
        <br><br>

        VPC Peering = Direct VPC-to-VPC connection
        <br><br>

        VPC Endpoint = Private access to supported AWS services
        <br><br>

        Transit Gateway = Central network hub
        <br><br>

        Flow Logs = Network traffic metadata for troubleshooting
    </strong>

    <br><br>

    <strong>ðŸ”¥ Production Flow</strong>

    <br><br>

    Users

    â†’

    Load Balancer

    â†’

    Public Subnets

    â†’

    Private App Subnets

    â†’

    Private DB Subnets

    <br><br>

    Private App

    â†’

    NAT Gateway

    â†’

    Internet Gateway

    â†’

    Internet

    <br><br>

    Security:

    IAM + Security Groups + NACLs

    <br>

    Monitoring:

    VPC Flow Logs + CloudWatch

<!-- LOAD BALANCING -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Load Balancing</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is Load Balancing?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
Load balancing distributes incoming application traffic across
multiple healthy servers or resources.
</p>

<div class="flow">

Users

â†“

<strong>Load Balancer</strong>

â†“

Server 1 Â Â  Server 2 Â Â  Server 3

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>
Suppose an application receives thousands of requests.

Instead of sending every request to one server, the load
balancer distributes traffic across multiple application
instances.

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Load balancing distributes incoming traffic across multiple
healthy resources. It improves availability, scalability and
fault tolerance by preventing a single server from handling all
the traffic."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>Why do we need a Load Balancer?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p>
A load balancer can help:

<br><br>
â†’ Distribute traffic <br>
â†’ Improve availability <br>
â†’ Support horizontal scaling <br>
â†’ Detect unhealthy targets <br>
â†’ Reduce dependency on a single server

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>
If Server-1 becomes unhealthy, the load balancer can stop
sending new requests to that unhealthy target and route traffic
to healthy targets.
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What is a Health Check?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
A health check verifies whether a target is healthy enough to
receive traffic.
</p>

<div class="flow">

Load Balancer

â†“

Health Check

â†“

Healthy â†’ Receive Traffic

Unhealthy â†’ Do Not Receive New Traffic

</div>

</article>

<!-- AUTO SCALING -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Auto Scaling</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>What is Auto Scaling?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the number or capacity of
resources according to workload requirements and configured
policies.
</p>

<div class="flow">

Low Traffic <br>
â†“
Fewer Instances <br>
â†“
Traffic Increases <br>
â†“
More Instances <br>
â†“
Traffic Decreases <br>
â†“
Scale Down

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes resources according
to workload demand. It helps maintain application performance
during traffic changes while avoiding unnecessary resource
usage."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>Scalability vs Auto Scaling?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table>

<tr>
<th>Scalability</th>
<th>Auto Scaling</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Ability to handle increased workload</td>
<td>Mechanism that automatically adjusts resources</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>General architecture capability</td>
<td>Automated resource adjustment</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Can be manual or automatic</td>
<td>Uses configured policies/rules</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Scalability is the ability of a system to handle increased
workload, while Auto Scaling is an automated mechanism that adds
or removes resources according to defined conditions."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<h3>What is Multi-AZ architecture?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
Multi-AZ architecture deploys application resources across

<div class="flow">

AWS Region

â†“

AZ-A Â Â Â Â  AZ-B

â†“

Application Instances

</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

single Availability Zone."
</p>

</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 07</div>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<div class="flow">

Users

â†“

Load Balancer

â†“

AZ-A Â Â Â Â  AZ-B

â†“

Application Instances

â†“

Database

I would distribute application instances across multiple

</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

Zones and place a load balancer in front of the application
instances. I would use health checks and Auto Scaling where

</p>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
DNS stands for Domain Name System.

<div class="flow">

â†“

DNS

â†“

â†“

<div class="answer">

<div class="number">QUESTION 16</div>

<h3>RPO vs RTO?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table>

<tr>
<th>RPO</th>
<th>RTO</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Recovery Point Objective</td>
<td>Recovery Time Objective</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>How much data loss is acceptable?</td>
<td>How much downtime is acceptable?</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Measured in time/data point</td>
<td>Measured in recovery time</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

RPO = 15 minutes

<br>
â†’ Business can tolerate losing up to around 15 minutes of
data.

<br><br>

RTO = 1 hour

<br>
â†’ Application should be restored within approximately 1 hour.

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"RPO defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured
in time, while RTO defines the target time within which a system
should be restored after a disruption."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<!-- WELL ARCHITECTED -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­ Cloud Architecture / Well-Architected</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 17</div>

<h3>What is the AWS Well-Architected Framework?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
The AWS Well-Architected Framework provides principles and best
practices for designing and evaluating cloud workloads.
</p>

<p>
The major pillars are:

<br><br>

â†’ Operational Excellence <br>
â†’ Security <br>
â†’ Reliability <br>
â†’ Performance Efficiency <br>
â†’ Cost Optimization <br>
â†’ Sustainability

</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"The AWS Well-Architected Framework provides best practices for
designing secure, reliable, efficient and cost-effective cloud
workloads. It is organized around six pillars: operational
excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost
optimization and sustainability."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 18</div>

<h3>Why is architecture important in Cloud?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Cloud architecture determines how resources are organized to
achieve availability, security, scalability, performance and
cost objectives.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Good cloud architecture balances availability, scalability,
security, performance and cost according to the application's
business requirements."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<!-- COMPLETE ARCHITECTURE -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Production Architecture</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<h3>How would you design a highly available web application?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<div class="flow">

Users

â†“

DNS

â†“

CDN / Edge

â†“

Load Balancer

â†“

â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â” <br>
AZ-A Â Â Â Â Â  AZ-B <br>
Application Â Â  Application <br>
Instances Â Â Â  Instances <br>
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜

â†“

Database

â†“

Backup / DR

</div>

<p>
For a production application, I would avoid depending on a
single server or Availability Zone.
</p>

<p>
I would use DNS for name resolution, a CDN when global content
delivery is required, a load balancer for traffic distribution,
multiple Availability Zones for resilience and Auto Scaling for
variable workload.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would design the application using a multi-tier and
multi-AZ architecture. DNS would route users to the application,
a CDN could serve cacheable content, and a load balancer would
distribute traffic across healthy application instances in
multiple Availability Zones. Auto Scaling would adjust capacity
based on demand. I would use an appropriate highly available
database configuration and implement backups and disaster
recovery according to the application's RPO and RTO
requirements."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- SCENARIOS -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>ðŸŽ¯ Real-Time Interview Scenarios</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 01</div>

<h3>
Traffic suddenly increases 10 times. What would you do?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
I would use horizontal scaling with a load balancer and Auto
Scaling.
</p>

<div class="flow">

Traffic Increase

â†“

Load Balancer

â†“

Auto Scaling

â†“

More Instances

â†“

Traffic Distributed

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would use a load-balanced architecture with Auto Scaling.
When demand increases, additional instances can be launched and
traffic can be distributed across healthy instances. When demand
falls, capacity can scale down."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 02</div>

<h3>
One Availability Zone goes down. How can the application remain available?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones and
use a load balancer to route traffic to healthy resources.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would deploy application instances across multiple
Availability Zones and use health checks with a load balancer.
If one AZ becomes unavailable, traffic can continue through
healthy resources in another AZ."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 03</div>

<h3>
Users from different countries complain about slow static content.
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
I would evaluate using a CDN so that cacheable content can be
served from edge locations closer to users.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would use a CDN for cacheable static content. The CDN can
serve content from geographically distributed edge locations,
reducing latency for users who are far from the origin."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 04</div>

<h3>
The business says the application must recover within 30 minutes and can tolerate only 5 minutes of data loss.
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ RTO/RPO</span>

<p>

RTO = 30 minutes

<br>

RPO = 5 minutes

</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>
"The recovery requirements are an RTO of 30 minutes and an RPO
of 5 minutes. I would design the backup and disaster recovery
strategy to meet those objectives."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 05</div>

<h3>
Should every application use Multi-Region architecture?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ TRICK QUESTION</span>

<p>
No.

Multi-Region architecture adds operational complexity and cost.
It should be selected when business requirements justify it.

</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>
"No. I would choose Multi-Region based on requirements such as
regional disaster recovery, geographic distribution, latency or
business continuity. For many applications, Multi-AZ provides
sufficient high availability within a region."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="section">
<h2>ðŸ§  Quick-Fire Questions</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<h3>Rapid Revision</h3>

<p>

<strong>Q:</strong> Load Balancer?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Distributes traffic across healthy resources.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Health Check?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Determines whether a target is healthy.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Auto Scaling?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Automatically adjusts resource capacity.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Multi-AZ?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Deploy resources across multiple AZs in one region.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Multi-Region?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Deploy workloads across multiple geographic regions.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> DNS?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Resolves domain names to addresses/endpoints.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> CDN?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Delivers content from locations closer to users.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Backup?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Copy of data used for restoration.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Disaster Recovery?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Process and architecture for restoring systems after disruption.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> RPO?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> RTO?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Target recovery time after disruption.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Well-Architected Framework?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Best-practice framework for designing and evaluating cloud workloads.

</p>

</article>

â†’ Copy of data for restoration.

<p>
Core cloud concepts, service models, deployment models,
scalability, elasticity, availability, regions, AZs and
real-time DevOps interview scenarios.
</p>

</header>

<main class="content">

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Very Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is Cloud Computing?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud computing means delivering computing resources such as
servers, storage, databases, networking and software over the
internet on demand.

Instead of buying and maintaining physical infrastructure,
organizations can consume cloud resources whenever they need
them.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

Suppose a company needs a server for its application.

Traditional approach:

<br><br>

Buy physical server â†’ Install it â†’ Maintain hardware â†’ Pay for
unused capacity.

<br><br>

Cloud approach:

<br><br>

Create an EC2 instance â†’ Deploy application â†’ Scale when needed
â†’ Pay according to usage.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of computing resources
such as compute, storage, networking and databases over the
internet, allowing organizations to provision resources quickly
without managing the underlying physical infrastructure."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>Why do companies use Cloud Computing?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

The main reason is that cloud allows organizations to provision
infrastructure quickly and scale resources according to workload.

Important benefits include:

<br><br>

â†’ On-demand resources

<br>
â†’ Scalability

<br>
â†’ Elasticity

<br>
â†’ High availability

<br>
â†’ Global reach

<br>
â†’ Reduced infrastructure management

<br>
â†’ Pay-as-you-go pricing models

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>

An e-commerce application may have normal traffic on weekdays
but extremely high traffic during a festival sale.

Cloud infrastructure can scale according to demand.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Companies use cloud computing because it provides on-demand
infrastructure, scalability, elasticity, high availability and
global deployment while reducing the need to manage physical
hardware."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What are the different Cloud Service Models?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

The three major cloud service models are:

<br><br>

<strong>IaaS â€” Infrastructure as a Service</strong>

<br>

<strong>PaaS â€” Platform as a Service</strong>

<br>

<strong>SaaS â€” Software as a Service</strong>

</p>

<div class="flow">

IaaS

â†’

You manage more infrastructure

<br><br>

PaaS

â†’

Cloud manages the platform

<br><br>

SaaS

â†’

You mainly consume the application

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>What is IaaS?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

IaaS stands for Infrastructure as a Service.

The cloud provider provides infrastructure resources such as
virtual machines, storage and networking.

The customer has more control over the operating system and
software stack.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ AWS Example</strong>

<p>

Amazon EC2 is a common example of IaaS.

You choose the instance type, operating system, networking,
storage and install your required software.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"IaaS provides infrastructure resources such as compute,
storage and networking. The customer manages the operating
system and applications while the cloud provider manages the
underlying physical infrastructure."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>What is PaaS?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

PaaS stands for Platform as a Service.

The cloud provider manages the underlying infrastructure and
platform components, allowing developers to focus more on the
application.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

Instead of creating a server, installing the operating system
and configuring the runtime yourself, a PaaS service can provide
the application platform and manage much of the infrastructure
for you.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"PaaS provides a managed application platform where the cloud
provider handles much of the infrastructure and platform
management, allowing developers to focus mainly on application
development and deployment."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 06</div>

<h3>What is SaaS?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

SaaS stands for Software as a Service.

The complete application is provided as a service over the
internet.

The customer generally consumes the application instead of
managing its underlying infrastructure.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Examples</strong>

<p>

Email services, online collaboration applications and CRM
software can be delivered as SaaS.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"SaaS is a cloud service model where a complete software
application is delivered to users over the internet, while the
provider manages the underlying infrastructure and application
platform."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 07</div>

<h3>What is the difference between IaaS, PaaS and SaaS?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<div class="important">

<strong>IaaS</strong> â†’ More infrastructure control.

<br><br>

<strong>PaaS</strong> â†’ Focus on application development.

<br><br>

<strong>SaaS</strong> â†’ Consume ready-to-use software.

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ§  Easy Memory</strong>

<p>

IaaS â†’ "Give me infrastructure."

<br>

PaaS â†’ "Give me a platform."

<br>

SaaS â†’ "Give me the software."

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"IaaS gives customers infrastructure resources with greater
control. PaaS provides a managed platform for application
development and deployment. SaaS provides a complete application
that users consume over the internet."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 08</div>

<h3>What are the Cloud Deployment Models?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

The commonly discussed deployment models are:

<br><br>

â†’ Public Cloud

<br>
â†’ Private Cloud

<br>
â†’ Hybrid Cloud

<br>
â†’ Community Cloud

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 09</div>

<h3>What is Public Cloud?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

In a public cloud, cloud infrastructure is provided by a cloud
provider and resources are delivered to customers over the
provider's platform.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Examples</strong>

<p>

AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud provide public cloud
services.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 10</div>

<h3>What is Private Cloud?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A private cloud environment is dedicated to a single
organization.

It can provide greater control over the environment and may be
operated by the organization or a service provider.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 11</div>

<h3>What is Hybrid Cloud?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Hybrid cloud combines private infrastructure with public cloud
resources and allows workloads or data to operate across both
environments.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>

A company keeps sensitive workloads in its private environment
while using AWS for scalable application infrastructure.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Hybrid cloud is an architecture that combines private
infrastructure with public cloud services. Organizations may use
it when they need a combination of control, compliance,
integration or public-cloud scalability."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­ High Priority</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 12</div>

<h3>What is Scalability?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Scalability is the ability of a system to handle increased
workload by increasing its resources or capacity.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

If an application needs more CPU or additional servers because
traffic increases, scaling the infrastructure allows the
application to handle the additional workload.

</p>

</div>

<div class="important">

<strong>Vertical Scaling</strong>

<br>

Increase the capacity of an existing resource.

<br><br>

<strong>Horizontal Scaling</strong>

<br>

Add more instances/resources.

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 13</div>

<h3>What is Vertical Scaling?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Vertical scaling means increasing the capacity of an existing
server or resource.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

EC2:

<br><br>

t3.medium â†’ larger instance type

<br><br>

The same server becomes more powerful.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 14</div>

<h3>What is Horizontal Scaling?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Horizontal scaling means adding or removing multiple instances
or resources to handle workload.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

1 EC2 instance

<br>
â†“

<br>

3 EC2 instances

<br>
â†“

<br>

Load Balancer distributes traffic.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Horizontal scaling increases capacity by adding more instances,
while vertical scaling increases the capacity of an existing
instance."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 15</div>

<h3>What is Elasticity?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Elasticity is the ability of a cloud environment to automatically
increase or decrease resources according to workload demand.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Low Traffic

â†’

Fewer Resources

â†’

Traffic Increases

â†’

More Resources

â†’

Traffic Decreases

â†’

Scale Down

</div>

<div class="important">

<strong>Memory Trick:</strong>

<br><br>

Scalability = ability to handle growth.

<br>

Elasticity = dynamically adjust resources according to demand.

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 16</div>

<h3>What is the difference between Scalability and Elasticity?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

A system is designed to support more users by adding
infrastructure â†’ <strong>Scalability</strong>.

<br><br>

The infrastructure automatically adds resources during peak
traffic and removes them after traffic decreases â†’ <strong>Elasticity</strong>.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Scalability refers to the ability of a system to handle
increased workload by increasing capacity. Elasticity goes one
step further by dynamically adding or removing resources based on
current demand."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 17</div>

<h3>What is High Availability?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

High availability means designing systems so that they remain
available and continue serving users even when some components
fail.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ AWS Example</strong>

<p>

Deploy application instances across multiple Availability Zones
and use a load balancer to distribute traffic.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 18</div>

<h3>What is Fault Tolerance?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Fault tolerance means the system can continue operating even when
one or more components fail.

</p>

<div class="important">

<strong>High Availability</strong>

â†’ Reduce downtime and remain available.

<br><br>

<strong>Fault Tolerance</strong>

â†’ Continue operation despite failures.

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 19</div>

<h3>What is an AWS Region?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

An AWS Region is a separate geographic area containing multiple
Availability Zones.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

Mumbai region:

<br>

<strong>ap-south-1</strong>

<br><br>

A region contains multiple Availability Zones that are isolated
from each other.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 20</div>

<h3>What is an Availability Zone?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

An Availability Zone, or AZ, is one or more discrete data
centers within an AWS Region, designed with independent
infrastructure to provide isolation and resilience.

</p>

<div class="flow">

AWS Region

â†“

Availability Zone A

Availability Zone B

Availability Zone C

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS
Region. Deploying workloads across multiple Availability Zones
helps improve availability and resilience."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 21</div>

<h3>Why do we deploy applications across multiple Availability Zones?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

To improve availability and reduce the impact of an Availability
Zone failure.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

If an application runs only in AZ-A and that AZ experiences an
issue, the application may become unavailable.

If workloads are distributed across AZ-A and AZ-B, traffic can
continue through healthy infrastructure.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 23</div>

<h3>What is Multi-Region Architecture?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Multi-Region architecture means deploying workloads across
multiple AWS Regions.

It can be used for disaster recovery, business continuity,
latency optimization or geographic requirements.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 24</div>

<h3>What is Disaster Recovery?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Disaster Recovery is the process and architecture used to restore
applications and data after a major failure or disaster.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

If the primary environment becomes unavailable, a company may
restore the application using backups or a secondary environment.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 25</div>

<h3>What is Pay-as-you-go?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Pay-as-you-go means customers generally pay for the cloud
resources they consume rather than purchasing all physical
infrastructure upfront.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

If you launch an EC2 instance for a workload, charges are based
on the applicable pricing model and usage.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<span class="label">â­â­</span>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 27</div>

<h3>What is Multi-Cloud?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Multi-cloud means using services from more than one cloud
provider.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

An organization may use AWS for infrastructure, Azure for

data or analytics workloads.

</p>

</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 28</div>

<h3>What is Vendor Lock-in?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Vendor lock-in occurs when it becomes difficult or expensive to
move workloads from one cloud provider or technology to another.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

An application heavily dependent on provider-specific services
may require significant redesign before it can be moved to
another cloud.

</p>

</div>

â†’

Load Balancer

â†’

â†’

More Instances

</p>

â†“

â†“

â†“

Database

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 04</div>

<h3>
Why would you choose Multi-AZ instead of Multi-Region?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

resilience within a region.

Multi-Region is considered when requirements include regional
disaster recovery, geographic distribution or global latency
needs.

</p>

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<!-- SHARED RESPONSIBILITY -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Shared Responsibility</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is the Shared Responsibility Model?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
The Shared Responsibility Model defines which security
responsibilities are handled by the cloud provider and which
responsibilities remain with the customer.
</p>

<div class="flow">

Cloud Provider <br>
â†“
Security <strong>OF</strong> the Cloud <br><br>
Customer <br>
â†“
Security <strong>IN</strong> the Cloud

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>
The cloud provider is responsible for physical data centers,
physical networking and underlying infrastructure.

The customer is responsible for things such as data,
identities, permissions and configuration according to the
service being used.

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"The Shared Responsibility Model defines how security
responsibilities are divided between the cloud provider and the
customer. The provider is responsible for security of the
underlying cloud infrastructure, while the customer remains
responsible for security and configuration within the cloud
according to the services they use."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>What does the cloud provider manage?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
The provider generally manages the underlying physical and
cloud infrastructure, including data centers, physical
hardware, networking infrastructure and foundational services.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"The provider manages the physical infrastructure and the
security of the underlying cloud environment, including data
centers, hardware and foundational infrastructure."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What does the customer manage?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Customer responsibilities depend on the service, but can include
data, identities, access permissions, application configuration,
operating systems for some services, network configuration and
security settings.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ EC2 Example</strong>

<p>
AWS manages the physical server and underlying infrastructure.

The customer manages the guest operating system, installed
software, IAM permissions, security configuration and application
data.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>Does the cloud provider secure everything automatically?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW TRICK QUESTION</span>

<p>
No.

Using a cloud provider does not remove the customer's security
responsibilities.

Incorrect IAM permissions, exposed storage, weak credentials,
insecure applications or misconfigured resources can still
create security risks.

</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>
"No. Cloud security is a shared responsibility. The provider
secures the underlying cloud infrastructure, but the customer
must securely configure identities, permissions, data and
resources according to the service."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<!-- IAM -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Cloud Identity & IAM</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>What is IAM?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
IAM stands for Identity and Access Management.

IAM controls:

<br><br>
â†’ Who can access resources <br>
â†’ What they can access <br>
â†’ What actions they can perform

</p>

<div class="flow">

Identity <br>
â†“
Authentication <br>
â†“
Authorization <br>
â†“
Resource Access

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
A DevOps engineer may be allowed to read logs and deploy
applications but may not be allowed to delete production
databases.
</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"IAM is used to manage identities and control access to cloud
resources. It determines who can access a resource and what
actions that identity is allowed to perform."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 06</div>

<h3>What is Authentication?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Authentication verifies the identity of a user, application or
system.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>
Username + password, MFA or another identity mechanism is used
to prove who you are.
</p>

</div>

<div class="note">

<strong>ðŸ§  Memory Trick</strong>

<br><br>
Authentication â†’ <strong>Who are you?</strong> <br>
Authorization â†’ <strong>What are you allowed to do?</strong>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 07</div>

<h3>What is Authorization?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Authorization determines what an authenticated identity is
allowed to access or perform.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
A user successfully logs in.

Authentication â†’ User is verified.

Authorization â†’ User is allowed to read an S3 bucket but not
delete objects.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 08</div>

<h3>Authentication vs Authorization?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table>

<tr>
<th>Authentication</th>
<th>Authorization</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Verifies identity</td>
<td>Determines permissions</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Who are you?</td>
<td>What can you do?</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Login / MFA</td>
<td>Policies / Permissions</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Authentication verifies who the user is, while authorization
determines what that authenticated user is allowed to access or
perform."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 09</div>

<h3>What is the Principle of Least Privilege?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p>
Least privilege means giving an identity only the permissions
required to perform its job and no unnecessary permissions.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>
A monitoring application only needs permission to read metrics.

It does NOT need permission to terminate EC2 instances.

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Least privilege means granting only the minimum permissions
required to perform a task. It reduces the impact of accidental
or unauthorized actions."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 10</div>

<h3>Why is MFA important?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
MFA, or Multi-Factor Authentication, adds an additional
verification factor beyond a password.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
Password + authenticator code.

Even if the password is compromised, the attacker may still
need the second factor.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 11</div>

<h3>What is a cloud IAM policy?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
An IAM policy is a set of permissions that defines which actions
are allowed or denied on specified resources under defined
conditions.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
Allow:

<br>
â†’ Read objects from a specific storage location.

Deny:

<br>
â†’ Delete objects.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Cloud Monitoring & Logging</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 12</div>

<h3>What is Cloud Monitoring?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
Cloud monitoring is the process of collecting and observing
metrics and health information from cloud resources and
applications.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>
Monitor:

<br>
â†’ CPU utilization
<br>
â†’ Memory
<br>
â†’ Network traffic
<br>
â†’ Request count
<br>
â†’ Error rate
<br>
â†’ Latency

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Cloud monitoring collects and analyzes metrics and health
information from infrastructure and applications so that teams
can detect problems, understand performance and take corrective
actions."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 13</div>

<h3>What is logging?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Logging records events and activities generated by systems,
applications and infrastructure.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
Application logs may contain:

<br>
â†’ Request information
<br>
â†’ Errors
<br>
â†’ Authentication events
<br>
â†’ Application events

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 14</div>

<h3>Monitoring vs Logging?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table>

<tr>
<th>Monitoring</th>
<th>Logging</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Observes metrics and health</td>
<td>Records events and messages</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>CPU = 90%</td>
<td>Application error message</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Helps identify performance problems</td>
<td>Helps investigate events and failures</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Monitoring focuses mainly on metrics and system health, while
logging records detailed events and messages. Monitoring can tell
me that something is wrong, while logs often help me understand
what happened."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 15</div>

<h3>What is an alert?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
An alert is a notification generated when a defined condition
or threshold is met.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>
CPU utilization > 80%

â†“

Monitoring detects threshold

â†“

Alert

â†“

DevOps engineer investigates

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 16</div>

<h3>Why is monitoring important in DevOps?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p>
Monitoring helps DevOps teams detect failures, identify
performance bottlenecks, understand system behavior and respond
to incidents.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Monitoring is important in DevOps because it provides visibility
into infrastructure and applications. It helps teams detect
issues early, troubleshoot incidents, measure performance and
improve reliability."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- DATABASE -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Cloud Database Fundamentals</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 17</div>

<h3>What is a cloud database?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p>
A cloud database is a database service hosted or managed within
a cloud environment.
</p>

<p>
Cloud databases can be relational or non-relational depending
on application requirements.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"A cloud database is a database service provided or hosted in a
cloud environment. Depending on the workload, organizations can
choose relational or non-relational database technologies."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 18</div>

<h3>What is a relational database?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p>
A relational database stores structured data in tables made up
of rows and columns and typically uses SQL for querying and
managing data.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

Customers table:

<br><br>

ID | Name | Email

<br>
1 | Nandu | nandu@example.com

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"A relational database stores structured data in tables with
rows and columns and commonly uses SQL. It is suitable for
workloads that require structured relationships and transactional
consistency."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 19</div>

<h3>What is a NoSQL database?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
NoSQL databases are non-relational databases designed for
flexible data models and large-scale distributed workloads.
Different NoSQL systems use models such as key-value,
document, column-family or graph.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
A user profile can be represented as a document containing
different attributes without requiring a fixed relational table
structure.
</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"NoSQL databases are non-relational databases designed for
flexible data models and scalable distributed workloads. They
are useful when the application does not require a traditional
relational table structure."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 20</div>

<h3>SQL vs NoSQL â€” What is the difference?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table>

<tr>
<th>SQL / Relational</th>
<th>NoSQL</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Tables and relationships</td>
<td>Flexible data models</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Structured schema</td>
<td>Often flexible schema</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>SQL queries</td>
<td>Database-specific query models</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Strong fit for relational transactions</td>
<td>Strong fit for many distributed/flexible workloads</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"Relational databases organize structured data into related
tables and use SQL, while NoSQL databases provide flexible data
models and are commonly used for horizontally scalable
distributed workloads. The choice depends on application
requirements."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 21</div>

<h3>What is a primary key?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a relational
table.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>
Customer ID can uniquely identify each customer.
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 22</div>

<h3>What is a database transaction?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
A transaction is a logical unit of database work that should be
processed according to the database's consistency and transaction
rules.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Banking Example</strong>

<p>

Transfer â‚¹1,000:

<br><br>

Debit Account A

â†“

Credit Account B

<br><br>

The transaction should not leave the system in an incorrect
partial state.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card">

<div class="number">QUESTION 23</div>

<h3>What is a managed database service?</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
A managed database service is a cloud database offering where
the provider handles many operational tasks such as
infrastructure provisioning, maintenance and certain backup or
patching operations depending on the service.
</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ AWS Example</strong>

<p>
Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service.

The provider handles many infrastructure-level operational
tasks, while the customer still manages database configuration,
data, access and other responsibilities depending on the
service.

</p>

</div>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>
"A managed database service reduces operational overhead by
having the cloud provider manage much of the underlying
infrastructure and database operations. The exact division of
responsibility depends on the service."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- SCENARIOS -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="section">
<h2>ðŸŽ¯ Real-Time Interview Scenarios</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 01</div>

<h3>
A developer needs access only to read application logs. What permissions would you give?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ LEAST PRIVILEGE</span>

<p>
I would create or use an identity with only the required
read-only permissions for the relevant logging resources.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would follow least privilege and provide only the read
permissions required for the relevant logs. I would avoid
granting write, administrative or resource-deletion permissions
because they are not required for the developer's task."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 02</div>

<h3>
An application suddenly becomes slow. How would monitoring help?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
I would check relevant metrics such as CPU, memory, network,
request count, latency, error rate and database performance.
Then I would correlate the metrics with logs to identify the
root cause.
</p>

<div class="flow">

User Reports Slowness

â†“

Monitoring Metrics

â†“

Identify Abnormal Metric

â†“

Application Logs

â†“

Root Cause

â†“

Fix / Scale / Optimize

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 03</div>

<h3>
A company needs strong relationships between customer, order and payment data. Which database type would you consider?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
A relational database would generally be a strong candidate
because the data has structured relationships and transactional
requirements.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would consider a relational database because customer, order
and payment information has structured relationships and may
require transactional consistency."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 04</div>

<h3>
An application has highly variable traffic and needs a highly scalable data store with a flexible data model. What would you consider?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p>
Depending on the workload, a NoSQL database could be considered
because many NoSQL systems are designed for distributed,
horizontally scalable workloads and flexible data models.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>
"I would evaluate a NoSQL database if the application requires a
flexible data model and large-scale distributed access. I would
still make the final choice based on consistency, access
patterns, query requirements and workload characteristics."
</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="card scenario">

<div class="number">SCENARIO 05</div>

<h3>
A cloud storage resource was accidentally made publicly accessible. Whose responsibility is that?
</h3>

<span class="priority">â­â­â­â­â­ SHARED RESPONSIBILITY</span>

<p>
The exact responsibility depends on the service, but incorrect
resource permissions and configuration are generally customer
responsibilities.
</p>

<div class="answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>
"Under the Shared Responsibility Model, the provider secures
the underlying cloud infrastructure, while the customer is
responsible for securely configuring resources, identities and
access permissions. Therefore, an incorrectly configured public
storage resource is generally a customer-side configuration
issue."
</p>

</div>

</article>

â†’ Who are you?

<strong>Authorization</strong>

â†’ What can you do?
