<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Very Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is Computer Networking?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Computer networking is the process of connecting computers,
servers, applications and other devices so that they can
communicate and exchange data.

In cloud environments, networking allows users, applications,
services and databases to communicate securely.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

A user opens a website.

<br><br>

User

â†“

Internet

â†“

Load Balancer

â†“

Application Server

â†“

Database

<br><br>

Networking allows communication between these different
components.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Computer networking is the communication between connected
devices and systems using defined protocols and addressing
mechanisms. In cloud environments, networking enables secure
communication between users, applications and services."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>What is an IP Address?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

An IP address is a logical address assigned to a network
interface or device so that it can be identified and
communicate over a network.

There are two major IP versions:

<br><br>

â†’ IPv4

<br>
â†’ IPv6

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ IPv4 Example</strong>

<p>

192.168.1.10

<br><br>

A server can use an IP address to communicate with other
systems on the network.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"An IP address is a logical network address used to identify a
network interface and enable communication between systems."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What is the difference between Public IP and Private IP?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Public IP</th>
<th>Private IP</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Used for communication over the public internet</td>
<td>Used inside private networks</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Must be globally unique within its scope</td>
<td>Can be reused in different private networks</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Used when direct public connectivity is required</td>
<td>Commonly used for internal communication</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Cloud Example</strong>

<p>

Web server:

Public-facing load balancer may have public connectivity.

<br><br>

Database:

Uses private connectivity and should generally not be directly
exposed to the public internet.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A public IP is used for public network communication, while a
private IP is used for communication within a private network.
In a secure cloud architecture, internal services such as
databases are commonly accessed using private networking."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>What is a subnet?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

A subnet is a logical subdivision of an IP network.

Subnets help organize resources and control how network traffic
flows within a larger network.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Cloud Example</strong>

<p>

A VPC can be divided into multiple subnets.

<br><br>

Public Subnet

â†’ Load Balancer

<br><br>

Private Subnet

â†’ Application Servers

<br><br>

Private Subnet

â†’ Database

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A subnet is a logical subdivision of an IP network. In cloud
architectures, subnets are commonly used to organize resources
and separate public-facing and internal workloads."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>What is a CIDR block?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

CIDR stands for Classless Inter-Domain Routing.

It is a notation used to represent a range of IP addresses.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

10.0.0.0/16

<br><br>

The <strong>/16</strong> represents the network prefix length.

<br><br>

Smaller prefix length â†’ generally larger address range.

<br>

Larger prefix length â†’ generally smaller address range.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"CIDR is a notation used to define IP address ranges using a
network prefix length, such as 10.0.0.0/16."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 06</div>

<h3>What is DNS?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

DNS stands for Domain Name System.

DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses
that systems can use to communicate.

</p>

<div class="flow">

User

â†“

[www.example.com](http://www.example.com)

â†“

DNS

â†“

IP Address

â†“

Web Server

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

Humans prefer:

<br>

google.com

<br><br>

Computers communicate using network addresses such as IP
addresses.

DNS provides the mapping between the domain name and the
appropriate address.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"DNS is a naming system that translates domain names into
network addresses, allowing users to access services using
human-readable names instead of IP addresses."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 07</div>

<h3>What is a Port?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

A port is a logical communication endpoint used by networked
applications and services.

Different services commonly listen on different port numbers.

</p>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Port</th>
<th>Common Usage</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>22</td>
<td>SSH</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>80</td>
<td>HTTP</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>443</td>
<td>HTTPS</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>53</td>
<td>DNS</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>3306</td>
<td>MySQL</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>5432</td>
<td>PostgreSQL</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A port is a logical endpoint used to identify a specific
network service or application on a host."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 08</div>

<h3>What is HTTP vs HTTPS?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>HTTP</th>
<th>HTTPS</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Hypertext Transfer Protocol</td>
<td>HTTP Secure</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Normally uses port 80</td>
<td>Normally uses port 443</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Traffic is not protected by TLS</td>
<td>Uses TLS to protect communication</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"HTTP is the standard protocol for transferring web data,
typically over port 80. HTTPS uses HTTP over TLS to provide
encrypted and authenticated communication, typically over
port 443."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 09</div>

<h3>What is TCP vs UDP?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>TCP</th>
<th>UDP</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Connection-oriented</td>
<td>Connectionless</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Reliable delivery</td>
<td>No built-in delivery guarantee</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Maintains ordering</td>
<td>Does not provide TCP-style ordering</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>More overhead</td>
<td>Lower overhead</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Understanding</strong>

<p>

TCP:

"Make sure the data reaches correctly."

<br><br>

UDP:

"Send the data quickly without establishing the same type of
connection and reliability mechanism."

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered
delivery, while UDP is connectionless and provides lower
overhead without TCP's built-in reliability and ordering
mechanisms."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 10</div>

<h3>What is a Router?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A router is a network device or function that forwards packets
between different networks based on routing information.

In cloud environments, routing tables determine how traffic
should move between network destinations.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Source

â†“

Router / Routing Table

â†“

Destination Network

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A router forwards network traffic between different networks
based on routing information. In cloud environments, routing
tables determine where packets should be sent."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 11</div>

<h3>What is a Firewall?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

A firewall is a security control that filters network traffic
according to defined rules.

Rules may determine which traffic is allowed or denied based on
factors such as source, destination, protocol and port.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

Allow:

â†’ HTTPS traffic to the web application.

<br><br>

Restrict:

â†’ Direct database access from the public internet.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A firewall controls network traffic by applying security rules
that allow or deny communication based on defined criteria."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 12</div>

<h3>What is a Load Balancer?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple
healthy backend resources.

It helps improve availability, scalability and reliability.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Users

â†“

Load Balancer

â†™ â†“ â†˜

Server 1   Server 2   Server 3

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>

Suppose one server cannot handle all requests.

Instead of sending every request to one server, a load balancer
distributes requests across multiple healthy servers.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple
backend resources, improving availability and allowing the
application to scale horizontally."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 13</div>

<h3>What is NAT?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

NAT stands for Network Address Translation.

It allows private network resources to communicate with external
networks by translating network addresses.

In AWS, a NAT Gateway is commonly used to allow resources in
private subnets to initiate outbound internet connections without
making those resources directly publicly reachable.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Private EC2

â†“

Private Subnet

â†“

NAT Gateway

â†“

Internet

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"NAT allows private resources to communicate with external
networks without requiring those resources to have direct public
internet exposure. In AWS, a NAT Gateway is commonly used for
outbound internet access from private subnets."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 14</div>

<h3>What is a VPN?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

VPN stands for Virtual Private Network.

It creates a secure communication path over an untrusted or
public network.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

A company has an on-premises data center and an AWS VPC.

A VPN connection can provide encrypted connectivity between the
two environments over the internet.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 15</div>

<h3>What is a private network?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A private network is a network environment intended for internal
communication and not directly exposed to the public internet.

Private networking is commonly used for backend services,
databases and internal applications.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 16</div>

<h3>What is the difference between public and private subnet?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Public Subnet</th>
<th>Private Subnet</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Has a route that provides a path to an Internet Gateway</td>
<td>Does not have a direct route to an Internet Gateway</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Can contain internet-facing resources when appropriately configured</td>
<td>Common for internal resources</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Example: public load balancer</td>
<td>Example: database / internal application</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Important</strong>

<br><br>

A subnet is considered public when its routing provides a path
to an Internet Gateway.

A public IP alone does not by itself define the subnet as public.

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 17</div>

<h3>What is an Internet Gateway?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

An Internet Gateway is an AWS VPC component that provides a path
for communication between resources in a VPC and the public
internet when the routing and addressing configuration allow it.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Public Subnet

â†“

Route Table

â†“

Internet Gateway

â†“

Internet

</div>

</article>

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 18</div>

<h3>What is a routing table?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A routing table contains rules that determine where network
traffic should be sent based on the destination address.

<div class="example">

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 19</div>

<h3>What is latency?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Latency is the time taken for data to travel between a source
and destination.

Lower latency generally means faster response times.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Cloud Example</strong>

<p>

If users are located in India, choosing infrastructure closer to
those users can reduce network latency compared with placing the
same workload much farther away.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 20</div>

<h3>What is bandwidth?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Bandwidth refers to the amount of data that can be transferred
over a network connection within a given period.

</p>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Easy Memory</strong>

<br><br>

Latency â†’ How long does it take?

<br>

Bandwidth â†’ How much data can be transferred?

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 21</div>

<h3>What is a network protocol?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A network protocol is a defined set of rules that systems use to
communicate with each other.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Examples</strong>

<p>

HTTP â†’ Web communication

<br>

HTTPS â†’ Secure web communication

<br>

TCP â†’ Reliable transport

<br>

UDP â†’ Connectionless transport

<br>

DNS â†’ Name resolution

<br>

SSH â†’ Secure remote administration

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­ Less Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 22</div>

<h3>What is packet loss?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Packet loss occurs when network packets fail to reach their
destination.

It can result in retransmissions, degraded performance,
timeouts or application errors depending on the protocol and
application.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 23</div>

<h3>What is a MAC address?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A MAC address is a hardware-level network identifier associated
with a network interface.

It operates at the data-link layer and is different from an IP
address.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 01</div>

<h3>
Your EC2 instance cannot access the internet. How will you troubleshoot it?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

I would troubleshoot the network path step by step instead of
randomly changing security rules.

</p>

<div class="flow">

EC2

â†“

Subnet

â†“

Route Table

â†“

NAT / Internet Gateway

â†“

Internet

</div>

<p class="answer">

Check:

<br><br>

â†’ Is the instance in the correct subnet?

<br>
â†’ Does the route table contain the required route?

<br>
â†’ If private subnet, is NAT configured correctly?

<br>
â†’ If public subnet, is an Internet Gateway attached and routed?

<br>
â†’ Are Security Group rules allowing required traffic?

<br>
â†’ Are Network ACL rules allowing traffic?

<br>
â†’ Is DNS resolution configured correctly if the issue is
domain-based?

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would troubleshoot from the instance outward: verify the
subnet and route table, then check the NAT Gateway or Internet
Gateway depending on the architecture, followed by Security
Group and NACL rules, DNS configuration and the destination
itself."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 02</div>

<h3>
The application server can reach the internet, but users cannot reach the application. What could be wrong?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

The outbound path working does not guarantee inbound public
connectivity.

I would check:

<br><br>

â†’ Load balancer / public endpoint

<br>
â†’ Public IP or DNS configuration

<br>
â†’ Route table

<br>
â†’ Internet Gateway path

<br>
â†’ Security Group inbound rules

<br>
â†’ NACL rules

<br>
â†’ Application listening port

</p>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 03</div>

<h3>
Your application can reach the EC2 server, but cannot connect to MySQL. How do you troubleshoot?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<div class="flow">

Application Server

â†“

Security Group

â†“

Network Path

â†“

Database Security Group

â†“

MySQL : 3306

â†“

Database

</div>

<p class="answer">

I would verify:

<br><br>

â†’ Database is running

<br>
â†’ Application uses correct database endpoint

<br>
â†’ Port 3306 is listening

<br>
â†’ Database Security Group allows port 3306 from the application
security group or appropriate source

<br>
â†’ NACL rules

<br>
â†’ Routing

<br>
â†’ Credentials and database configuration

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would first confirm the database is healthy and listening on
the expected port. Then I would verify the network path, routing,
database Security Group rules, NACLs and finally the application
credentials and connection configuration."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 04</div>

<h3>
How would you design a secure three-tier cloud network?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<div class="flow">

ðŸŒ Internet

â†“

Public Load Balancer

â†“

Private Application Subnet

â†“

Private Database Subnet

<br><br>

Security Groups

*

Routing

*

NACLs

*

IAM

*

Encryption

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would place only the required internet-facing component in
the public layer, keep application and database workloads in
private subnets, control traffic between tiers using security
groups, use appropriate routing and network controls, and
protect sensitive data with encryption."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 05</div>

<h3>
Why should a database usually not be placed directly in a public subnet?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A database usually does not need direct internet access.

Keeping it private reduces its public attack surface and allows
access to be restricted to trusted application components.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would normally keep the database in private subnets because
it does not require direct internet exposure. Application
servers can communicate with it through controlled private
network paths and security-group rules."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>ðŸ§  Quick-Fire Interview Questions</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<h3>Rapid Revision</h3>

<p class="answer">

<strong>Q:</strong> What is an IP address?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Logical network address used for communication.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Public IP?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Address used for public network communication.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Private IP?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Address used within private networks.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Subnet?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Logical subdivision of an IP network.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> CIDR?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Notation used to represent IP address ranges.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> DNS?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Translates domain names into network addresses.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Port?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Logical communication endpoint for a service.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> HTTP?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Web protocol, normally port 80.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> HTTPS?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> HTTP protected with TLS, normally port 443.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> TCP?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Connection-oriented and reliable transport protocol.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> UDP?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Connectionless transport protocol with lower overhead.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Firewall?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Filters network traffic according to rules.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Load Balancer?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Distributes traffic across backend resources.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> NAT?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Provides address translation; commonly enables private
resources to initiate outbound connectivity.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> VPN?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Secure network connection over an untrusted network.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Latency?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Time taken for data to travel between endpoints.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> Bandwidth?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Amount of data that can be transferred over a
connection in a given period.

</p>

</article>

<h1>Cloud Pricing & <span>Cost Optimization</span></h1>

<p>
Understand how cloud services are charged, how organizations
control cloud spending, and how to answer real-world
cost-optimization questions in DevOps interviews.
</p>

</header>

<main class="content">

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Very Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is the Pay-as-you-go model in Cloud Computing?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Pay-as-you-go means paying for the cloud resources you consume
according to the applicable pricing model and usage instead of
purchasing all infrastructure upfront.

You can provision resources when required and stop or remove
them when they are no longer needed.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

A company needs an EC2 server for a temporary project.

Instead of purchasing a physical server, it launches an EC2
instance and pays according to the applicable EC2 pricing model
and usage.

When the workload is finished, the resource can be terminated.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Pay-as-you-go is a cloud pricing approach where customers pay
for the resources they consume according to the service's
pricing model, rather than making a large upfront investment in
physical infrastructure."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>What are the major Cloud Pricing Models?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Common cloud purchasing/pricing options include:

<br><br>

â†’ On-Demand

<br>
â†’ Reserved capacity / Reserved Instances

<br>
â†’ Savings Plans

<br>
â†’ Spot Instances

<br>
â†’ Free Tier where applicable

</p>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Easy Memory</strong>

<br><br>

On-Demand â†’ Flexibility

<br>

Reserved â†’ Commitment

<br>

Savings Plans â†’ Flexible commitment to usage

<br>

Spot â†’ Use spare cloud capacity at variable discounted pricing,
with interruption risk

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What is On-Demand pricing?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

On-Demand pricing allows you to use eligible cloud resources
without a long-term commitment.

You pay according to the service's applicable usage-based pricing.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

You need an EC2 instance for a short-term development workload.

You can launch it without committing to a long-term purchase
model.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"On-Demand pricing provides flexibility because there is no
long-term capacity commitment. It is useful for short-term,
unpredictable or changing workloads."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>What are Reserved Instances?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Reserved Instances are a purchasing option for certain AWS
services where you make a commitment for a defined term in
exchange for discounted pricing compared with equivalent
On-Demand usage.

The exact discount and flexibility depend on the service and
reservation configuration.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>

Suppose a production workload requires a stable compute
capacity for a long period.

Instead of using only On-Demand pricing, the organization may
consider a suitable reservation to reduce the effective compute
cost.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Reserved Instances are a commitment-based purchasing option
that can provide lower effective pricing for predictable
workloads compared with On-Demand usage."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>What are AWS Savings Plans?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Savings Plans provide discounted pricing in exchange for a
commitment to a consistent amount of eligible usage, measured
per hour, over a specified term.

They can offer more flexibility than traditional instance
reservations depending on the Savings Plan type.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

An organization has predictable compute usage but may change
instance families or move workloads between eligible compute
services.

A suitable Savings Plan may provide more flexibility while
reducing effective compute cost.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 06</div>

<h3>What is a Spot Instance?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

A Spot Instance uses spare AWS compute capacity and can provide
significant discounts compared with On-Demand pricing.

The important point is that Spot capacity can be interrupted by
AWS when the capacity is needed back.

Therefore, Spot is best suited for workloads that can tolerate
interruption.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Good Use Cases</strong>

<p>

â†’ Batch processing

<br>

â†’ Fault-tolerant workloads

<br>

â†’ Data processing

<br>

â†’ Flexible background jobs

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Spot Instances use spare AWS compute capacity at discounted
pricing. Because the capacity can be interrupted, I would use
Spot for fault-tolerant or interruptible workloads rather than
critical workloads that require uninterrupted compute."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 07</div>

<h3>What is the difference between On-Demand, Reserved and Spot?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<table>

<tr>
<th>Option</th>
<th>Main Idea</th>
<th>Best For</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>On-Demand</td>
<td>Flexible usage without long-term commitment</td>
<td>Short-term / unpredictable workloads</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Reserved</td>
<td>Commitment for discounted effective pricing</td>
<td>Predictable workloads</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Spot</td>
<td>Spare capacity at discounted pricing</td>
<td>Interruptible workloads</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"On-Demand is best when flexibility is important. Reserved
capacity can reduce cost for predictable workloads with a
commitment. Spot is useful for fault-tolerant workloads that can
handle interruption."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 08</div>

<h3>What is CapEx vs OpEx?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

<strong>CapEx</strong> means Capital Expenditure.

It is spending on assets that generally require upfront
investment, such as purchasing physical servers and data-center
equipment.

<br><br>

<strong>OpEx</strong> means Operational Expenditure.

It refers to ongoing operating costs.

Cloud computing commonly shifts much infrastructure spending
from large upfront capital purchases toward usage-based
operational spending.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

Traditional data center:

<br>

Buy servers â†’ CapEx

<br><br>

Cloud:

<br>

Consume cloud resources â†’ Operating expense model

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"CapEx is upfront investment in physical assets such as servers
and data-center infrastructure. OpEx is ongoing operational
spending. Cloud computing can reduce large upfront infrastructure
investment by using usage-based operating expenses."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 09</div>

<h3>What is Cloud Cost Optimization?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud cost optimization means controlling cloud spending while
still meeting application performance, availability, security
and business requirements.

The goal is not simply to make everything as cheap as possible.

The goal is to get the required business value from the cloud
with efficient resource usage.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

If a development EC2 instance runs 24/7 even though developers
use it only during working hours, scheduling it to stop outside
working hours can reduce unnecessary cost.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Cloud cost optimization is the continuous process of reducing
unnecessary cloud spending while maintaining the required
performance, reliability, security and business outcomes."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<!-- â­â­â­â­ -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­ High Priority</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 10</div>

<h3>How can you reduce AWS costs?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Some common approaches are:

<br><br>

â†’ Right-size resources

<br>
â†’ Stop unused development resources

<br>
â†’ Delete unused EBS volumes and snapshots where appropriate

<br>
â†’ Use appropriate commitment-based pricing for predictable
workloads

<br>
â†’ Use Spot for suitable interruptible workloads

<br>
â†’ Use Auto Scaling

<br>
â†’ Monitor costs continuously

<br>
â†’ Apply tags for cost allocation

<br>
â†’ Review storage lifecycle policies

<br>
â†’ Remove unused resources

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would start by identifying unused and underutilized
resources, then right-size them. I would use Auto Scaling,
appropriate purchasing options for predictable workloads, Spot
where suitable, storage lifecycle policies, tagging and
continuous cost monitoring."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 11</div>

<h3>What is Right-Sizing?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Right-sizing means selecting the appropriate resource size for
the actual workload instead of over-provisioning resources.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

Suppose monitoring shows an application consistently uses very
little CPU and memory on a large instance.

Moving to an appropriately sized instance may reduce cost while
still meeting performance requirements.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Right-sizing means matching cloud resource capacity to actual
workload requirements. It helps avoid paying for unused
capacity."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 12</div>

<h3>Why is Auto Scaling useful for Cost Optimization?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Auto Scaling can increase capacity when demand increases and
reduce capacity when demand decreases.

This helps avoid running more resources than required.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Low Traffic

â†’

Fewer Instances

â†’

Traffic Increases

â†’

More Instances

â†’

Traffic Decreases

â†’

Scale Down

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 13</div>

<h3>How do unused resources increase cloud costs?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud resources can continue generating charges while they are
provisioned even if they are not actively being used, depending
on the service and resource.

Examples include idle compute resources, unattached storage and
unnecessary snapshots.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>

A developer creates several EC2 instances for testing and
forgets to terminate them after testing.

Those resources may continue generating charges.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 14</div>

<h3>What is AWS Cost Explorer?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

AWS Cost Explorer is a tool used to analyze and visualize AWS
cost and usage data.

It can help identify spending trends, services contributing to
costs and changes over time.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"I use Cost Explorer to analyze AWS spending and usage trends,
identify major cost drivers and investigate unexpected changes
in cost."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 15</div>

<h3>What are AWS Budgets?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

AWS Budgets allows organizations to create custom cost and usage
budgets and receive notifications when actual or forecasted
spending crosses defined thresholds.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

A project team can create a monthly budget and configure an
alert when spending reaches a defined percentage of that budget.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 16</div>

<h3>What is resource tagging and why is it useful for cost management?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Tags are key-value metadata attached to supported cloud
resources.

Organizations can use tags such as:

<br><br>

Environment = Production

<br>

Project = ECommerce

<br>

Team = DevOps

<br>

Owner = Nandu

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Cost Example</strong>

<p>

If multiple teams use the same AWS account, tags can help
attribute eligible costs to projects, environments or teams.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<!-- â­â­â­ -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­ Medium Priority</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 17</div>

<h3>What is FinOps?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

FinOps is a collaborative practice that brings together
engineering, finance and business teams to manage cloud costs
and maximize business value from cloud usage.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Understanding</strong>

<p>

Developers understand the technical workload.

<br>

Finance understands spending.

<br>

Business understands the required value.

<br><br>

FinOps helps these teams make better cloud spending decisions
together.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 18</div>

<h3>What is the difference between Cost Optimization and Cost Cutting?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Cost cutting focuses primarily on reducing spending.

Cost optimization focuses on getting the required business
value at the most efficient cost while maintaining required
performance, security and reliability.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Cost optimization is not simply reducing the bill. It is
finding the most efficient architecture and resource usage while
still meeting business and technical requirements."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 19</div>

<h3>Why should development resources be stopped when not needed?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Development and testing environments may not need to run 24/7.

Stopping resources outside working hours can reduce unnecessary
usage-based costs for eligible services.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

Development environment:

<br>

9 AM â†’ Start

<br>

7 PM â†’ Stop

<br><br>

Instead of running continuously.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<!-- â­â­ -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­ Less Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 20</div>

<h3>What is a Cost Allocation Tag?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A cost allocation tag is a tag that can be used to organize or
attribute eligible cloud costs to categories such as projects,
departments or environments.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 21</div>

<h3>Why should you monitor cloud costs continuously?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud environments are dynamic. Resources can be created,
scaled or changed frequently.

Continuous monitoring helps identify unexpected spending,
resource waste and unusual cost patterns early.

</p>

</article>

<!-- ðŸŽ¯ SCENARIOS -->

<!-- ===================================================== -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>ðŸŽ¯ Real-Time Interview Scenarios</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 01</div>

<h3>
Your AWS bill suddenly increased this month. What will you do?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

I would not immediately delete resources.

First I would identify the cost increase and determine which
service, account, region or resource is responsible.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Cost Increase

â†“

Cost Explorer

â†“

Identify Cost Driver

â†“

Check Resource Usage

â†“

Find Root Cause

â†“

Right-Size / Stop / Change Pricing Model

â†“

Monitor Again

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"First I would use AWS cost analysis tools to identify the
service and usage responsible for the increase. Then I would
check whether the increase is expected or caused by unused,
misconfigured or over-provisioned resources. After identifying
the root cause, I would right-size resources, remove
unnecessary resources or select a more appropriate purchasing
model, and finally monitor the cost to verify the improvement."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 02</div>

<h3>
A development EC2 instance runs 24/7 but is used only during office hours. What will you do?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

For a development environment, I would consider an automated
schedule to stop the instance outside working hours and start it
again when required, provided the workload supports this.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would automate start and stop schedules for the development
environment so that compute resources are not running when they
are not needed. I would also verify dependencies and ensure
stopping the instance does not affect required data or services."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 03</div>

<h3>
Your production workload runs continuously and has predictable usage. Which pricing approach would you investigate?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

I would evaluate commitment-based pricing such as Reserved
Instances or an appropriate Savings Plan, depending on the
service and workload characteristics.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>

"Because the workload is stable and predictable, I would analyze
its historical usage and evaluate a suitable commitment-based
pricing option. I would compare the effective cost and
flexibility before making the decision."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 04</div>

<h3>
You have a batch-processing workload that can tolerate interruption. What would you consider?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

I would consider Spot Instances for eligible compute workloads
because the workload can tolerate interruption.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>

"Since the workload is fault-tolerant and can tolerate
interruption, I would evaluate Spot capacity to reduce compute
cost. I would also design the workload so it can recover or
restart if capacity is interrupted."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 05</div>

<h3>
Your EC2 instance is very large but monitoring shows consistently low utilization. What will you do?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

I would analyze CPU, memory, network and application performance
requirements before choosing a smaller instance.

This is a classic right-sizing opportunity.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would review historical utilization and application
requirements and select a smaller instance only if it can still
meet performance and reliability requirements. This is called
right-sizing."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>ðŸ§  Quick-Fire Interview Questions</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<h3>Rapid Revision</h3>

<p class="answer">

<strong>Q:</strong> What is Pay-as-you-go?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Pay according to applicable resource usage and pricing.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is On-Demand?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Flexible usage without long-term commitment.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What are Reserved Instances?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Commitment-based purchasing option for predictable workloads.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is a Savings Plan?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Commitment to eligible usage in exchange for discounted pricing.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is Spot?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Spare capacity at discounted pricing with interruption risk.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is Right-Sizing?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Matching resource capacity to actual workload requirements.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is Cost Optimization?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Efficiently managing cloud spending while meeting technical and business requirements.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is Cost Explorer?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Tool for analyzing AWS cost and usage.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What are AWS Budgets?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Tool for setting cost/usage budgets and receiving alerts.

<br><br>

<strong>Q:</strong> What is FinOps?

<br>
<strong>A:</strong> Collaborative approach to managing cloud financial efficiency.

</p>

</article>

<h1>Cloud Security <span>Fundamentals</span></h1>

<p>
Understand the security principles behind cloud environments,
identity, access control, encryption, network protection and
real-world DevOps security scenarios.
</p>

</header>

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Very Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is Cloud Security?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud security is the set of technologies, processes,
policies and controls used to protect cloud resources,
applications, identities and data from unauthorized access,
misconfiguration, attacks and other security threats.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

An application is running on AWS.

Cloud security may involve:

<br><br>

â†’ IAM controls who can access resources

<br>
â†’ Security Groups control network access

<br>
â†’ Encryption protects data

<br>
â†’ Logging helps detect suspicious activity

<br>
â†’ Least privilege limits unnecessary permissions

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Cloud security is the practice of protecting cloud
infrastructure, applications, identities and data using
appropriate security controls, policies and processes."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>What is the Shared Responsibility Model?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

The Shared Responsibility Model defines which security
responsibilities are handled by the cloud provider and which
responsibilities are handled by the customer.

The exact division depends on the cloud service being used.

</p>

<div class="flow">

<strong>CLOUD PROVIDER</strong>

â†“

Security OF the Cloud

â†“

Physical Infrastructure

Data Centers

Hardware

Networking Infrastructure

<br><br>

<strong>CUSTOMER</strong>

â†“

Security IN the Cloud

â†“

Data

Identity & Access

Configurations

Operating System where applicable

Applications

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ AWS Example</strong>

<p>

AWS is responsible for protecting the physical infrastructure
and underlying cloud infrastructure.

The customer is responsible for correctly configuring resources,
controlling access and protecting their data.

For an EC2 instance, the customer also has responsibility for
the guest operating system and software they install.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"The Shared Responsibility Model divides security
responsibilities between the cloud provider and the customer.
The provider is responsible for security of the underlying
cloud infrastructure, while the customer is responsible for
security controls within their environment, such as data,
identity, configuration and, depending on the service, the
operating system and applications."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What is the difference between Authentication and Authorization?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

<strong>Authentication</strong> verifies who you are.

<br><br>

<strong>Authorization</strong> determines what you are allowed
to do after you are authenticated.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

You log in to AWS.

<br>

Authentication:

â†’ "Are you really Nandu?"

<br><br>

Authorization:

â†’ "What AWS resources is Nandu allowed to access?"

</p>

</div>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Authentication</th>
<th>Authorization</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Who are you?</td>
<td>What can you do?</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Verifies identity</td>
<td>Checks permissions</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Login / identity verification</td>
<td>Policies / permissions</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Authentication verifies the identity of a user or system,
while authorization determines what actions that authenticated
identity is permitted to perform."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>What is the Principle of Least Privilege?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

The Principle of Least Privilege means giving a user, service
or application only the permissions required to perform its
intended task and no unnecessary permissions.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Real-Time Example</strong>

<p>

Suppose a CI/CD pipeline only needs permission to push an image
to Amazon ECR.

Instead of giving the pipeline administrator-level access to
the entire AWS account, provide only the required permissions.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Least privilege means granting only the minimum permissions
required for a user or application to perform its task. It
reduces the potential impact if credentials are compromised."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>What is IAM?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

IAM stands for Identity and Access Management.

It is used to control who can access cloud resources and what
actions they are allowed to perform.

</p>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Remember</strong>

<br><br>

Identity â†’ Who is accessing?

<br>

Authentication â†’ Are they really who they claim to be?

<br>

Authorization â†’ What can they do?

<br>

IAM â†’ Manage identities and permissions.

</div>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ AWS Example</strong>

<p>

A developer may need permission to read objects from a specific
S3 bucket but should not automatically receive permission to
delete the entire AWS infrastructure.

</p>

</div>

<p class="answer">

AWS IAM is covered separately in this guide in much greater
depth. Here the focus is the fundamental security concept.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 06</div>

<h3>What is Encryption?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Encryption converts readable data, called plaintext, into an
encoded form, called ciphertext, so that unauthorized parties
cannot easily understand it.

A cryptographic key is used as part of the encryption and
decryption process.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

Sensitive customer data is stored in a database.

If the data is encrypted at rest, someone who gains access to
the underlying encrypted data cannot simply read it as normal
plaintext.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Encryption protects data by transforming plaintext into
ciphertext using cryptographic mechanisms. Authorized systems
can decrypt the data using the appropriate key."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 07</div>

<h3>What is the difference between Encryption at Rest and Encryption in Transit?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Encryption at Rest</th>
<th>Encryption in Transit</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Protects stored data</td>
<td>Protects data while moving</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Disk / database / object storage</td>
<td>Network communication</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Example: encrypted storage</td>
<td>Example: HTTPS / TLS</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="flow">

Data Stored

â†’

ðŸ” Encryption at Rest

<br><br>

Application

â†’

ðŸ” TLS / HTTPS

â†’

Server

<br>

ðŸ” Encryption in Transit

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Encryption at rest protects data while it is stored, while
encryption in transit protects data while it is moving between
systems, such as between a client and server using TLS."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 08</div>

<h3>What is Multi-Factor Authentication?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Multi-Factor Authentication, or MFA, requires more than one
authentication factor to verify a user's identity.

Common factor categories include:

<br><br>

â†’ Something you know

<br>
â†’ Something you have

<br>
â†’ Something you are

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

Password + authentication code from an authenticator device.

Even if the password is compromised, the second factor adds
another security layer.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"MFA strengthens authentication by requiring multiple
independent authentication factors, reducing the risk of account
compromise from a stolen password."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 09</div>

<h3>What is a Security Group?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

In AWS, a Security Group acts as a virtual firewall for
associated resources such as EC2 instances.

It controls allowed inbound and outbound network traffic based
on configured rules.

Security Groups are stateful.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

Web server:

<br>

HTTP/HTTPS â†’ Allow from appropriate sources

<br>

SSH â†’ Allow only from a trusted administrative source

<br><br>

You should avoid exposing administrative ports broadly to the
internet unless there is a justified requirement.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"An AWS Security Group acts as a virtual firewall for supported
resources such as EC2. It controls inbound and outbound traffic
using rules and is stateful."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 10</div>

<h3>What is a Network ACL?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A Network ACL, or NACL, is a network-level access control
mechanism associated with a VPC subnet.

AWS Network ACLs are stateless, so return traffic must be
explicitly allowed by the appropriate rule.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A Network ACL is a stateless network access control layer
associated with a subnet. It can allow or deny traffic based on
rules."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 11</div>

<h3>Security Group vs Network ACL â€” What is the difference?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Security Group</th>
<th>Network ACL</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Works at resource level</td>
<td>Works at subnet level</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Stateful</td>
<td>Stateless</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Supports allow rules</td>
<td>Supports allow and deny rules</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Commonly associated with EC2</td>
<td>Associated with subnet</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Easy Memory</strong>

<br><br>

Security Group â†’ Stateful â†’ Resource

<br>

NACL â†’ Stateless â†’ Subnet

</div>

</article>

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­â­ High Priority</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 12</div>

<h3>Why should you avoid using the root user for daily AWS tasks?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

The AWS account root user has extensive privileges.

Using it for everyday operations increases security risk.

Instead, organizations should use appropriate IAM identities
and permissions for normal tasks.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would avoid using the AWS root user for daily operations
because it has highly privileged access. I would use appropriate
IAM identities with least-privilege permissions and protect the
root account with strong security controls such as MFA."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 13</div>

<h3>Why should AWS credentials not be hard-coded in source code?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

Hard-coding credentials in source code can expose secrets through
Git repositories, logs, build artifacts or accidental sharing.

Credentials should be managed using appropriate secret and
identity mechanisms.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>âŒ Bad Practice</strong>

<p>

Password or access key directly inside application source code.

<br><br>

<strong>âœ… Better Approach</strong>

Use appropriate IAM roles, secret-management mechanisms and
temporary credentials where possible.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would never hard-code cloud credentials in source code.
Depending on the workload, I would prefer IAM roles or an
appropriate secrets-management mechanism and use least
privilege."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 14</div>

<h3>What is a secret?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A secret is sensitive information that should be protected from
unauthorized access.

Examples include:

<br><br>

â†’ API keys

<br>
â†’ Database passwords

<br>
â†’ Tokens

<br>
â†’ Private credentials

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ DevOps Example</strong>

<p>

A CI/CD pipeline needs a database password.

Instead of placing the password inside the Git repository, store
it in an appropriate secrets-management system and provide
access only to the required workload.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 15</div>

<h3>What is the Principle of Defense in Depth?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Defense in Depth means using multiple independent security
controls so that if one security layer fails, additional layers
can still provide protection.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Identity Controls

â†“

Network Controls

â†“

Encryption

â†“

Application Security

â†“

Logging & Monitoring

â†“

Incident Response

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Defense in Depth means implementing multiple security layers
instead of relying on a single control. If one layer fails,
other controls can reduce the impact."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 16</div>

<h3>Why is logging important for cloud security?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Security logs help organizations detect suspicious activity,
investigate incidents, understand what happened and support
auditing.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

If an unexpected administrative action occurs, logs can help
identify:

<br><br>

â†’ Who performed the action

<br>
â†’ What action occurred

<br>
â†’ When it occurred

<br>
â†’ Which resource was affected

</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- â­â­â­ -->

<!-- ================================================= -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­â­ Medium Priority</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 17</div>

<h3>What is a Zero Trust security approach?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Zero Trust is a security approach based on the principle that
access should not be automatically trusted simply because a
user or system is inside a particular network.

Access should be continuously evaluated based on identity,
context, permissions and other security controls.

</p>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Easy Memory</strong>

<br><br>

"Never automatically trust. Verify access."

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 18</div>

<h3>What is data masking?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Data masking hides or transforms sensitive information so that
unauthorized users cannot see the original sensitive values.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>Example</strong>

<p>

Production customer data may contain sensitive information.

A testing environment can use masked or anonymized values
instead of exposing the original production data.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 19</div>

<h3>Why should security patches be applied regularly?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Security patches fix known vulnerabilities and reduce the
opportunity for attackers to exploit outdated software.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would maintain a patching process for operating systems,
applications and dependencies based on risk and organizational
requirements. Critical vulnerabilities should be prioritized."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<!-- ================================================= -->

<!-- â­â­ -->

<!-- ================================================= -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>â­â­ Less Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 20</div>

<h3>What is a vulnerability?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A vulnerability is a weakness in software, configuration,
process or infrastructure that could potentially be exploited
by an attacker.

</p>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 21</div>

<h3>What is a security incident?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

A security incident is an event that may compromise the
confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems or data,
or indicates a potential security violation.

</p>

</article>

<!-- ðŸŽ¯ SCENARIOS -->

<!-- ================================================= -->

<div class="priority-title">
<h2>ðŸŽ¯ Real-Time Interview Scenarios</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 01</div>

<h3>
A developer asks for AdministratorAccess because their application is failing. What will you do?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

I would not immediately grant administrator access.

First I would identify what operation is failing and determine
the exact permission required.

Then I would provide the minimum required permission.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Application Error

â†“

Identify Failed Action

â†“

Identify Required Permission

â†“

Grant Minimum Permission

â†“

Test

â†“

Monitor

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would follow least privilege. Instead of granting
AdministratorAccess, I would identify the exact API action or
resource causing the failure and provide only the required
permission. If the permission is temporary, I would also
consider temporary access and review it afterward."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 02</div>

<h3>
An EC2 server is exposed to SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. Is this a good practice?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

Generally, allowing SSH from the entire internet unnecessarily
increases exposure.

I would restrict administrative access to trusted sources or use
a more appropriate secure access mechanism based on the
architecture.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Answer</strong>

<p>

"No, I would avoid exposing SSH to 0.0.0.0/0 unless there is a
specific justified requirement. I would restrict the source
range or use a secure administrative access solution and follow
least privilege."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 03</div>

<h3>
A GitHub repository contains an AWS access key. What will you do?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ CRITICAL</span>

<p class="answer">

I would treat the credential as compromised.

I would immediately revoke or rotate the exposed credential,
investigate its usage, identify the affected resources and
replace the authentication mechanism with a safer approach.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Secret Exposed

â†“

Revoke / Rotate

â†“

Check Usage / Logs

â†“

Assess Impact

â†“

Replace Hard-coded Credential

â†“

Use Secure Identity / Secret Management

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would treat the credential as compromised. I would
immediately revoke or rotate it, investigate logs for suspicious
usage, assess the impact and then remove the secret from the
repository history where appropriate. For the future, I would
use IAM roles or an appropriate secrets-management solution
instead of hard-coded credentials."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 04</div>

<h3>
An application needs to access an S3 bucket. Would you give the application full AWS access?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

No.

The application should receive only the permissions required
for its S3 operations.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

If the application only needs to read objects from one bucket,
the identity should not automatically receive permissions to
delete objects from every S3 bucket.

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question scenario">

<div class="question-number">SCENARIO 05</div>

<h3>
How would you secure a three-tier application in AWS?
</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ DEVOPS FAVORITE</span>

<p class="answer">

A common approach is to separate the web, application and
database tiers and restrict communication between them.

</p>

<div class="flow">

Internet

â†“

Load Balancer

â†“

Web / Application Tier

â†“

Application Tier

â†“

Database Tier

<br><br>

IAM + Least Privilege

*

Security Groups

*

Encryption

*

Logging & Monitoring

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Strong Answer</strong>

<p>

"I would separate the tiers and avoid exposing the database
directly to the internet. I would use appropriate network
controls between tiers, least-privilege IAM, encryption for
sensitive data, secure secrets management and logging and
monitoring for detection and auditing."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<br>

<br><br>

<h2>â­â­â­â­â­ Very Frequently Asked</h2>
<div class="line"></div>
</div>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 01</div>

<h3>What is Cloud Storage?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud storage is a service that allows organizations to store
data on infrastructure managed by a cloud provider.

Instead of purchasing and maintaining physical storage hardware,
organizations can provision storage according to their
requirements.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Simple Example</strong>

<p>

Traditional:

<br>
Buy storage hardware â†’ Install â†’ Maintain â†’ Expand manually

<br><br>

Cloud:

<br>
Create storage â†’ Upload data â†’ Increase capacity when required

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Cloud storage is the use of provider-managed storage
infrastructure to store and access data over a network. It
allows organizations to provision storage on demand without
managing the underlying physical storage hardware."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 02</div>

<h3>What are the major types of cloud storage?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

The three major storage models are:

<br><br>

â†’ Object Storage

<br>
â†’ Block Storage

<br>
â†’ File Storage

</p>

<table class="compare">

<tr>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Common Use</th>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Object Storage</td>
<td>Files, images, videos, backups, logs</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>Block Storage</td>
<td>Operating systems, databases, application disks</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>File Storage</td>
<td>Shared file systems and directories</td>
</tr>

</table>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"The three major cloud storage types are object, block and file
storage. Object storage is commonly used for unstructured data,
block storage provides disk-like storage for compute workloads,
and file storage provides shared file-system access."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 03</div>

<h3>What is Object Storage?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

Object storage stores data as objects.

An object generally contains:

<br><br>

â†’ Data

<br>
â†’ Metadata

<br>
â†’ Unique identifier / key

<br><br>

Object storage is designed for large amounts of unstructured
data.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ AWS Example â€” S3</strong>

<p>

An application receives user profile images.

Instead of storing those images directly on the application
server, the application can store them in object storage.

<br><br>

Application

â†“

Object Storage

â†“

Images / Videos / Backups

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Object storage stores data as objects along with metadata and
an identifier. It is well suited for large-scale unstructured
data such as images, videos, backups and logs."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 04</div>

<h3>What is Block Storage?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Block storage provides storage in the form of blocks that can be
attached to compute resources and used like disks.

It is commonly used when applications require low-latency,
persistent disk storage.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ AWS Example â€” EBS</strong>

<p>

An EC2 instance can use an EBS volume as its disk.

<br><br>

EC2

â†“

EBS Volume

â†“

Operating System / Application / Database

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Block storage provides disk-like storage that can be attached
to compute resources. It is commonly used for operating systems,
applications and databases that require persistent block-level
storage."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 05</div>

<h3>What is File Storage?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­</span>

<p class="answer">

File storage provides data through a hierarchical file-system
structure containing files and directories.

It is useful when multiple systems need shared access to the
same file system.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ AWS Example â€” EFS</strong>

<p>

Multiple application servers can mount the same shared file
system.

<br><br>

EC2-A â”€â”

<br>

EC2-B â”€â”¼â†’ Shared File Storage

<br>

EC2-C â”€â”˜

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"File storage provides a shared hierarchical file system. It is
useful when multiple compute resources need to access the same
files and directories."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 06</div>

<h3>Object vs Block vs File Storage â€” What is the difference?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ INTERVIEW FAVORITE</span>

<table class="compare">

<th>Block</th>
<th>File</th>

<td>Stores files/directories</td>
</tr>

<td>Disk-like workloads</td>
<td>Shared file-system workloads</td>

</tr>

</table>

<div class="important">

<strong>ðŸ§  Easy Memory</strong>

<br><br>

Object â†’ "Store files as objects."

<br><br>

Block â†’ "Give me a disk."

<br><br>

File â†’ "Give me a shared file system."

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Object storage is ideal for large-scale unstructured data,
block storage behaves like a disk for compute workloads, and
file storage provides shared file-system access."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 07</div>

<h3>What is the difference between durability and availability?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ VERY COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

These two terms are frequently confused.

<strong>Durability</strong> refers to how well a storage service
protects data against loss or corruption over time.

<strong>Availability</strong> refers to how accessible the service
or data is when users need it.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Easy Example</strong>

<p>

Durability:

"Will my data remain safe?"

<br><br>

Availability:

"Can I access the data when I need it?"

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Durability describes the likelihood that stored data will be
preserved without loss, while availability describes how
consistently the storage service can be accessed."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 08</div>

<h3>What is a backup?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

A backup is a separate copy of data created so that the data can
be restored after accidental deletion, corruption, operational
mistakes or other failures.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ”¥ Example</strong>

<p>

Production Database

â†“

Scheduled Backup

â†“

Backup Storage

<br><br>

If the database is accidentally deleted or corrupted, the backup
can be used for recovery.

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A backup is a separate copy of data maintained for recovery
purposes. It helps restore data after accidental deletion,
corruption or other failures."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 09</div>

<h3>What is a snapshot?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ COMMON</span>

<p class="answer">

A snapshot is a point-in-time representation of the state of
storage.

Snapshots can be used to create recoverable copies of storage
resources and can also be used as a basis for creating new
storage resources depending on the service.

</p>

<div class="example">

<strong>ðŸ’¡ Example</strong>

<p>

Database volume at 10:00 AM

â†“

Snapshot

â†“

Later data becomes corrupted

â†“

Create/restore storage from an appropriate snapshot

</p>

</div>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"A snapshot is a point-in-time copy or representation of a
storage resource that can be used for recovery, cloning or other
storage-management operations depending on the service."

</p>

</div>

</article>

<article class="question">

<div class="question-number">QUESTION 10</div>

<h3>Why is backup important in cloud environments?</h3>

<span class="label">â­â­â­â­â­ MUST KNOW</span>

<p class="answer">

Cloud infrastructure reduces the need to manage physical
hardware, but it does not automatically protect organizations
from every type of data loss.

Data can still be deleted accidentally, corrupted, overwritten
or affected by application-level mistakes.

Therefore, backups are an important part of a disaster recovery
strategy.

</p>

<div class="interview-answer">

<strong>ðŸŽ¤ Interview Answer</strong>

<p>

"Cloud providers provide highly resilient infrastructure, but
customers still need appropriate backup and recovery strategies
to protect against accidental deletion, corruption and
application-level failures."

</p>

</div>

</article>
